clue.text: This person, 50, outwardly shy, good-looking

indicators.note: outwardly says the word for shy sits on the outside, wrapped round the other pieces

parts.note: shy means coy, bashful
the setter referring to themself gives ME
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A bashful fifty-year-old who happens to be handsome describes themself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is crossword shorthand for the setter, so ME; with L it goes inside COY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person who is attractive in appearance; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Strike outside to end

parts.note: to strike can mean to cut, as with a blow or a blade
off can mean away from or outside, as in off the premises

explanation.surface: Workers walk out on strike, picketing outside until the dispute ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a supply or a conversation abruptly is to stop it short, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Temporary force — workers over the night period?

parts.note: to force someone to do something is to make them do it
a night shift is the team of workers on duty through the night

explanation.surface: A stopgap labour force is brought in, perhaps staffing the overnight hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift is a stopgap, used for the time being until a proper version arrives.

clue.text: Departed around start of night with sailors following light

indicators.note: following puts the sailors after what has gone before
around says the word for departed is placed round the next piece

parts.note: the departed are the dead, so departed can mean late

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of night

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, the British navy, so sailors

explanation.surface: Someone sets off as night falls, with a crew of seamen tagging along behind a light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departed' looks like 'left' but means LATE (dead); N goes inside it, giving LANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, a source of illumination carried by hand.

clue.text: Brief stay in hotel? That must be pots!

parts.note: the word stop turned over, that is reversed, reads pots, so the clue's last word is what the answer's two parts describe

explanation.surface: A guest makes a short hotel visit and exclaims that the kitchen pans are to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, STOP turned OVER, and it produces 'pots'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a short break in a journey, often a night spent at a hotel en route.

clue.text: Deceived worker could be so looked after …

parts.note: to be deceived is to be taken in, fooled
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand or deckhand

explanation.surface: A labourer who has been fooled might, the clue suggests, end up being cared for.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next one, which leans on the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken in hand is brought under someone's control and care, an idiom for being managed.

clue.text: … As could be this computer

parts.note: the ellipsis carries over the previous answer's phrase: this small machine is designed to be held and used in one hand

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a computer is said to share the fate of the fooled worker.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the previous answer literally: a device held in the hand, a handheld computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmtop is a handheld computer small enough to sit in the hand while used.

clue.text: One making choice against old books with little hesitation

parts.note: V stands for versus, meaning against
OT is the Old Testament, the older books of the Bible
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone picks a side against old volumes after a brief pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter is a person who casts a ballot, choosing between candidates.

clue.text: Fugitives manage when crossing path

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it

indicators.note: crossing says the word for when lies across, that is around, the word for path

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
a way is a path or route

explanation.surface: Escaped convicts get by as they cut across a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Runaways are people who have fled, escapees on the run.

clue.text: Accepting a ruler after short time

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the letter for time

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch takes the throne shortly afterwards and accepts the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something offered means receiving or agreeing to it, a synonym in participle form.

clue.text: Framework that's minimal, somehow not sleek

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of not sleek come together in some other order

explanation.surface: A frame that is bare-bones, though somehow lacking a sleek look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges NOT SLEEK; the definition covers both senses, a frame and a minimal version (skeleton staff).
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is a bare supporting structure, and as a modifier it means reduced to the minimum.

clue.text: One hoping for a catch in the deep?

definitions.text: One hoping for a catch in the deep?

parts.words: One hoping for a catch in the deep?
parts.note: reads like a fielder hoping to hold a catch in the deep, a cricket outfield position, but describes someone angling at sea

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder stationed far out on the boundary waits for a high ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket 'the deep' is the outfield near the boundary; here it is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler casting a line at sea hopes to land fish, a catch from the ocean.

clue.text: Plot to achieve speed of sound at start of race

indicators.note: at start of puts the speed figure at the front of the word for race

parts.note: Mach one, written MACH I, is the speed of sound
a race can mean a people or nation

explanation.surface: A scheme to break the sound barrier right at the start of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to achieve' is a link; MACH I uses the Roman numeral I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A machination is a crafty scheme or intrigue, a synonym for a secret plan.

clue.text: The unending quarrel produced by project

indicators.note: unending means the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: An endless dispute is the result of some scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To project something is to hurl or cast it forward, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Rave-up devoid of drugs? This person may have been wronged

definitions.meaning: a rave-up is a wild party, and one free of drugs would be blameless

definitions.text: This person may have been wronged
definitions.meaning: in a divorce or lawsuit, the blameless side who suffered the wrong

explanation.surface: A drug-free party turns out to involve someone treated unfairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally, the blameless participant in a dispute; literally, a clean, harmless celebration.

clue.text: Jumble in dream so puzzling

indicators.note: puzzling suggests the letters of in dream so are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Things get mixed up in a dream that is so baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: To randomise is to mix things into no order, a synonym for shuffle as a verb.

clue.text: Parish had somehow to avoid a disaster

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of parish had are rearranged
to avoid says the letter a is left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A parish somehow had to steer clear of catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' and 'to avoid' work together: take PARISHHAD, drop one A, and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is severe suffering or adversity, close to a calamity.

clue.text: Tyrannical writer meets Italian heretic

parts.note: an author is a writer
an Arian was a follower of Arius, whose teaching the early Church condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: A domineering novelist encounters an Italian dissenter from church doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Authoritarian means demanding strict obedience, as a despotic ruler does.

clue.text: Dance that was a significant thing for first man on moon

definitions.meaning: a lively ballroom dance in quick march time

definitions.text: that was a significant thing for first man on moon
definitions.meaning: Neil Armstrong called his first lunar footfall a small move for a man but a giant leap for mankind

explanation.surface: A dance is linked to Neil Armstrong's famous words on the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick ballroom dance shares its name with a single pace, Armstrong's famous footfall.

clue.text: Something that may be burning in awful scene

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of the word scene that follows are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Something is ablaze in a dreadful scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in' as a preposition joining definition to scene; it is a letter-giving piece, kept as written before the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Incense is an aromatic substance burnt for its fragrant smoke.

clue.text: State a thing that's sure to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the phrase is spoken and sounds like another word

parts.note: a cert is a certainty, a thing that is sure to happen

explanation.surface: Say something that is bound to be listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to declare firmly, a verb synonym for stating.

clue.text: Plunge into water from window senselessly

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in window senselessly

explanation.surface: Someone senselessly leaps out of a window into water.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'winDOW SEnselessly'; DOWSE is a variant spelling of douse.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to drench or immerse, a variant spelling of douse.

clue.text: City's water supplies

definitions.meaning: City's reads as 'city is': a small cathedral city in Somerset, England
sources of water dug or drilled into the ground

explanation.surface: A city's water supply is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells is an English cathedral city; wells are bored shafts reaching groundwater.

clue.text: Daring USA duo involved with CIA

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of usa duo and cia are tangled together

explanation.surface: A bold American pair works alongside the Central Intelligence Agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles USA DUO and CIA together; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacious means bold and willing to take risks.

clue.text: Breed of cattle torn apart by the lions

indicators.note: torn apart suggests the letters of the lions are pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: A herd animal is mauled by lions.
explanation.definitionFit: Holstein is a black-and-white dairy cow, a named breed.

clue.text: Herb may be entertained by women divers

indicators.note: entertained by says the answer is held within the words women divers

explanation.surface: A garden plant might be hosted by female divers.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy salad plant, loosely called a herb in crosswords.

clue.text: Put off job, one involving little power

indicators.note: involving says the job and one together enclose the letter for power

parts.note: a post is a job
taken as written
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Someone delays a task, the one with only a little authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone is to defer or delay to a later time.

clue.text: Moderate slope skier initially missed

indicators.note: missed says a letter is dropped from the word for slope

parts.note: a descent is a downward slope

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of skier

explanation.surface: A gentle slope that a skier skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like a verb but is an adjective: fair or acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent here means reasonable or satisfactory, a fair amount.
